_doc: Rules of the trainer prototype (feel numbers live here, not in code): combat (gauge, combo, stagger, swaps, channelling), control, terrain, ai_tiers, progression, sync (lens tiers), battle (arenas, trainers), temperament (route), hall, team, items (route only), partner (following on the route), wild (scaling), camp, materials, upgrades, spawn, guide.

guide.text: Gate Hall: set your team at the station (right), then walk through a gate
In battle YOU are your creature: left click moves, right click attacks, Space dodges
Physical moves fill the gauge; specials spend it. They're skillshots: lead your shots
Hold a status move to channel it: stronger the longer you hold, but a hit cancels it
Fill the gold stagger bar: a staggered foe takes 50% more
Take the door on the right to the route: wild creatures, the Sync Lens, a rival
Weaken or stagger a wild creature, then hold F: the trainer syncs it
Try every gate on Easy, Normal and Hard

white_out.text: Your team is worn out. You hurry back to camp, and they recover by the fire.

combat._doc: The gauge (physical hits fill it, specials spend it), the basic combo, stagger, swaps and channelling. bonus_cap: element + terrain + buffs together add at most this much damage.

sync._doc: The Sync Lens in an arena: F on a weakened (dazed) wild creature starts a scan of `scan` seconds (faster with a better lens). The creature struggles (telegraphed lunges at your creature every `struggle_every` s); a hit on your creature breaks the scan, retry after `retry` s.

terrain._doc: Arena features (ArenaLayout) and how they change. Destroying terrain changes the fight, never ends it: it costs a move, it transforms (grass burns -> ash and smoke -> burnt field -> regrows; rock -> rubble; bridge -> water; cracked floor -> pit), effects stay local, walls, ledges and deep water never break. states: how long each passing state lasts (s) and its sound.

ai_tiers._doc: How well the opponent plays. Only DECISION-MAKING (equal footing: the same stats, moves, wind-ups, gauge and rules as yours). react: seconds before it responds; pace: seconds it waits between attacks; dodge: chance to dodge your wind-ups; lead: how well it leads shots (0 aims at you, 1 at where you'll be); cover: chance to step behind cover when hurt; grass: chance to hide in grass; high_ground: chance to climb a ledge when you are at range; swap_below: a trainer swaps out under this life; counter_swap: swaps into an element advantage; save_gauge: waits for a full gauge or a stagger to spend; status: chance to channel its status move; channel: how long it channels (share of max). bait: chance to step into your range when you have gauge and dodge your move; push: chance to get on the far side of you from a hazard; deny: chance to burn or flatten your home terrain under you.

battle._doc: Arena battles: transition time, how wild opponents are picked in the Gate Hall, rewards, trainers. quick_win_levels: walking into a wild creature this many levels below your active one beats it on the spot (no arena; not an alpha).

lines.ask: Gate Warden: Three of mine against three of yours?
Ivo: Hey, new trainer! Want to battle?
lines.win: Ivo: Wow. Your partner really trusts you.
lines.lose: Ivo: Come back when you've trained some more!

temperament._doc: Wild creatures on the route never force a fight (walking into one starts it). warn: a territorial one warns at this range and calms after `calm_after` s if you back off; flee_range: a shy one runs from you; chase_range: an aggressive one (rare, red eye glint) chases.

trainer_shouts._doc: Short lines from the trainer at the arena edge (flavour). gap: at most one every this many seconds.

arena_view._doc: Creatures render (and their bodies are) `creature_scale` times bigger in arenas. The camera fits the arena plus `margin` px; `hud` px at the bottom stay clear for the cards.

alpha._doc: Rare bigger wild creatures: drawn and built `scale` times bigger with a glow, more life and power, their signature move as an extra attack (`attack`: its tell), and better rewards (`rewards` x XP and materials). One waits on the route; the Gate Hall's switch can send one.
